contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #285: Counterexamples to Baum–Connes and Kadison–Kaplansky.
Verify or refute the entire simultaneous-overlap chain in the staged September 23, 2026 irrational-trace manuscript, under exactly its graphical and adjustable-diagram hypotheses.

definitions.copies: Source-identified translates of finite connected simple regular reduced-labelled relator graphs, with isometric vertex embeddings and globally unique sufficiently long simple-path labels
definitions.minimality: Lexicographically minimize bounded faces then original edges over connected plane multigraph diagrams and adjustable exterior walks with fixed side endpoints and assignments; marks are contour positions
definitions.overlap: For one fixed c_P-to-root geodesic with first group vertex a, control all P intersect Q with Q!=P and d(c_Q,R)<=d(c_P,R); R is a group vertex or center, R!=c_P

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 285 (Counterexamples to Baum–Connes and Kadison–Kaplansky.; papers: A torsion-free counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes injectivity; A torsion-free counterexample to the Kadison–Kaplansky projection conjecture; An irrational-trace counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.
A genuinely publishable mathematical result, with verified novelty if claimed, passes the Host's independent Reviewer; overlap verification alone does not certify the campaign or any main theorem.
There exist a finitely generated group G and a scalar projection b in C_r^*(G) with irrational canonical trace, whose K0 class is outside coefficient-free proper reduced assembly.
There exists a finitely generated torsion-free group with a scalar reduced-algebra projection of canonical trace strictly between zero and one half.

There exists a finitely generated torsion-free group containing an embedded torus with integral orientation detector, but with its rank-zero Bott class zero in reduced K0; the torus Dirac class has infinite order and zero reduced assembly image.

Resolve the exact simultaneous-overlap dependency by a universal proof or an admissible exact counterexample. The DAG currently follows the universal-proof alternative; the other route is not required as an additional obligation.
An exact counterexample to a named overlap-chain assertion satisfies all applicable graphical hypotheses, and proves lexicographic minimality if it uses a minimal-diagram assertion.
Under the exact geometry hypotheses, different indexed copies do not share a simple path of length at least lambda times either source girth, and different indices give different subgraphs.

Every inflated coned loop admits a finite connected plane multigraph diagram with the prescribed exterior side occurrences and bounded contours assigned to translated relator copies; lexicographic minimizers in faces and then edges exist.

The minimal-diagram face omission, equal-copy mergers, unmarked-leaf deletion, bounded-face bridge deletion, and inverse-pair folding preserve the applicable side data and assignments and improve the claimed lexicographic complexity.

In every lexicographically minimal adjustable-side diagram, bounded faces have perimeter at least their assigned girth; every incident compressed arc is shorter than lambda times that girth, and generator-side arcs have unit length.

For a compressed minimal diagram with m prescribed sides, b arcs and F bounded faces, Euler and valence counting give v-b+F=1, 2b>=3(v-m), and F/lambda<=2b, including trees and isolated marked vertices.
Every such diagram satisfies (1/lambda-6)F<=6m-6 and b<=6m for 0<lambda<=1/12.

For an avoiding path closed by one designated P side, no arc has both exterior incidences in that same linear side occurrence; the bridge excursion deletion respects marked positions even when marked vertices are revisited.
If a coned edge path of length L joins x,a in P and avoids c_P, then d_P(x,a)<=12(L+1)lambda*sigma(P).
Every coned edge loop of length n>0 has a filling using at most 12n closed relations of perimeter at most four, with constants independent of the graphs, alphabet and lambda.

The standard linear coarse isoperimetric criterion converts uniform bounded-mesh linear fillings of a geodesic metric space into a thin-triangle constant depending only on those filling constants, without a local-finiteness assumption.
There exists an integer D0 independent of lambda, the graphs and the alphabet such that every vertex of a geodesic triangle in the coned graph is within D0 of a vertex on another side.

In the coned graph, assuming vertex D0-thinness, fix A=c_P!=R and one A-to-R geodesic with first group vertex a. If Q!=P, x in P intersect Q and d(c_Q,R)<=d(A,R), an A-avoiding walk from x to a has length at most L0=4D0+8, including equal-distance centers and either allowed root type.

With universal D0, t=D0+3 and L0=4D0+8, every intersection of P with a different Q whose center is no farther from the root than c_P lies in the same intrinsic induced P-ball about the first vertex a of one fixed root geodesic, of radius floor(12(L0+1)lambda*sigma(P)).
The labelled expander and parameter choices in data.tex:prop:data exist, including isometric embeddings, uniform expansion, sufficiently small induced tree balls, and diverging code-dimension gaps.
The ordinary finite-support cycle space of X over F2 is the internal algebraic direct sum of the cycle spaces of all indexed copies.
The finite-field codes with prescribed words, dimensions and primal/dual distance used in module.tex exist.
The globally generated relation module W0 has W0 intersect F_p^P equal to C_P perpendicular for every copy P.
The compact-dual restriction to each copy is exactly the prescribed code and has uniform Haar marginal, with prescribed-word probability p^(-k_i).
The enabled-graph construction makes designated valid copies pairwise disjoint isolated expander components and gives the asserted local deficits elsewhere.
For every enabled remaining graph and every finite vertex set Y, d|Y|-2|E(Y)| >= (c/2)|Y|, including the projected-cycle localization and disjoint cycle-rank charges.
The Fourier/crossed-product realization identifies the asserted fiber operators with a faithful reduced representation and gives the canonical trace integral.
The self-adjoint enabled-graph operator has the asserted kernel and the uniform gap min(rho,c^2/(8d)) on its complement in all relevant reduced fibers.
Continuous functional calculus of the uniformly gapped reduced operator gives the actual scalar projection b0 in C_r^*(V semidirect Gamma), with the asserted fiber diagonals.
The projection has trace sum_i p^(-k_i), which is irrational by the non-eventually-periodic base-p expansion.

For every countable discrete group, the canonical trace on every integral degree-zero coefficient-free proper reduced assembly class is rational, with the exact assembly comparison used by the manuscript.
The tower, path-recovery labelling, pruning and nilpotent voltage covers give the claimed embedded copies, common-root domains, forest complement and torsion-free finitely generated group.
Finite voltage and matrix-weight sampling simultaneously enforce the girth conditions and full regular-norm approximation to the nilpotent fiber model.
The local upper band survives removal of overlaps and the unused forest edges to give a uniformly separated, nonempty global reduced matrix spectral band.
The global upper spectral projection has strictly positive unnormalized matrix trace less than one half, including the weighted losses from all indexed copies.
The quantitative reduced free-product compression converts the small matrix projection to a scalar projection of the same trace while preserving torsion-freeness and finite generation.
The layered labelling, sequential expansion, pruning, Heisenberg voltage cover and common-root domains produce the claimed torsion-free finitely generated group with embedded torus.
An integral degree-two class restricts to the oriented torus generator and detects the torus Dirac K-homology class as infinite order.
The localized rank-zero Bott families are bounded operators and admit the required even/odd and odd/positive-even norm-continuous homotopies.
The finite sampled group-algebra operators and homotopies approximate the Bott model in the asserted reduced regular norm quotient.
The cancellation in the norm quotient yields an actual finite witness to vanishing of the embedded torus Bott class in one reduced group algebra.
The compact-support K-homology conventions, torus Dirac/Bott identification and reduced assembly naturality give an infinite-order assembly kernel class from the detector and analytic vanishing.

external_assumptions.statement: A geodesic metric space admitting a uniform bounded-mesh linear coarse isoperimetric inequality is hyperbolic, quantitatively in the filling constants and without local finiteness.
external_assumptions.source: Bridson and Haefliger, Metric Spaces of Non-Positive Curvature (1999); exact source passage not yet obtained, so this citation remains unchecked.

claims.natural_statement: A simply connected 2-complex with 2-cell attaching lengths at most M and linear combinatorial isoperimetric constant C has delta-hyperbolic 1-skeleton, with delta depending only on M and C and with no local-finiteness or bounded-valence assumption.

retired_assumptions.reason: The exact BH source was not obtained; the proof now uses the directly read combinatorial criterion in Groves--Manning Proposition 2.23 and an explicit disk-diagram bridge instead. No assertion that BH is false is made.

external_assumptions.source: Groves and Manning, Dehn filling in relatively hyperbolic groups, arXiv:math/0601311v4, 28 March 2009, Proposition 2.23, page 11. A separate read-only source researcher opened the full primary version; independent ledger attribution remains pending.

claims.natural_statement: The source-bound rational LP has exact minimum min(4m-b)=6, and the saved affine and root-constant certificates prove the stated numerical implications for every admissible value of their premises; this assertion does not certify the topological premises.
Under all original geometry hypotheses, every nontrivial minimal adjustable-side diagram has b<=4m-6 and (1/lambda-6)F<=4m-6; the isolated case has F=b=0 and is handled separately.
Under all original geometry hypotheses, every c_P-avoiding coned edge path of length L>=1 with endpoints x,a in P satisfies d_P(x,a)<=(4L-2)lambda*sigma(P); for L=0 the distance is zero.

Under all original geometry hypotheses, every coned edge loop of length n>0 is a product of at most 8n conjugates of closed edge relations of perimeter at most four, giving the corresponding combinatorial disk area bound even with singular intermediate contours.

Under all original geometry hypotheses there is a universal integer vertex-thinness constant D0 independent of lambda. For every allowed root R!=c_P and one fixed c_P-to-R geodesic with first group vertex a, all P intersect Q with Q!=P and d(c_Q,R)<=d(c_P,R) lie in the same intrinsic induced P-ball about a of radius floor((16D0+30)lambda*sigma(P)).
